pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 4.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READERS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how the main characters make the story flow. What would you consider when selecting a storybook to read?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the main characters in a text
2. explain how the characters make the story flow
3. appreciate the role of characters in the class reader

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 4.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READERS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 4.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READERS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the main characters in a text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the main characters in a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the main characters in a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the main characters in a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain how the characters make the story flow

What this means
In this part you learn to explain how the characters make the story flow. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain how the characters make the story flow.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain how the characters make the story flow. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of characters in the class reader

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of characters in the class reader. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of characters in the class reader.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of characters in the class reader. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the main characters in a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers to a partner. (skill: explain how the characters make the story flow)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of characters in the class reader)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the main characters in a text.
3. Practise this skill: explain how the characters make the story flow.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of characters in the class reader.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how the main characters make the story flow. What would you consider when selecting a storybook to read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the main characters in a text.
5. Be able to: explain how the characters make the story flow.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
